summary: The first lighthouse lit on the US West Coast (1 June 1854), at the mouth of the Golden Gate; the 1909 concrete tower still shines over the former prison island.

access.note: NPS lists the lighthouse as not open to the public; the island is a unit of Golden Gate National Recreation Area.

notes_for_editor: Wreck entry for Autocrat has no date (the 1893 report only says the buoy was discontinued). Tower height disagrees: 90 ft (LighthouseFriends), 95 ft (NPS), 84 ft (Preservation Project; USLHS also 84 ft base to lantern), record 26.0 m. 1906 log entry: marker credits B.F. Leeds, LighthouseFriends and roster put H.W. Young in office. Schneider's arrival role differs (LF first assistant, roster second assistant). Roster identification of Rushnell/Bushnell is by spelling variant only, stated as such. Edward Schneider's later death is omitted deliberately. LighthouseFriends dates the second northwest bell to 1900; the Board's fiscal 1901 report is cited instead. The NPS wayside text about a 1871 coal tram and steam siren was not used because it seemed to concern another site. Lighthouse Board volumes cited by scan page; printed pages unconfirmed. No newspapers read: the Chronicling America search timed out. Current characteristic (Fl W 5s in the record) not sourced here. Matched by position in OCR: none.
